title: Solar Radiation Warning
explanation: A real archived solar flare inspires this fictional warning. Protect the crew while keeping the colony supplied.
concept: A flare classification is not a radiation dose at Mars. Shielding and time indoors reduce modeled exposure.
uncertainty: The colony dose is illustrative. We do not know a Mars surface dose from this flare record.

title: Martian Dust Storm
explanation: Dust is blocking sunlight. Your arrays will produce less energy for three sols. Protect your battery and breathable air.
concept: Dust scatters and absorbs light. Solar generation falls, so batteries and load priorities become important.
uncertainty: The historical tau informs a simplified attenuation model. Local conditions and array design would change the real output.

title: Oxygen System Malfunction
explanation: A production unit has stopped. Stored oxygen and the emergency reserve give you time to restore it.
concept: Oxygen in a tank buys repair time. It does not by itself guarantee safe cabin pressure or remove carbon dioxide.
uncertainty: Repair times and equipment failure are simulated; no NASA mission reported this colony fault.

title: Greenhouse Failure
explanation: A failed climate controller has stopped one greenhouse. Use stored food while you decide how to recover.
concept: Plants need controlled temperature, water and energy. A cold outside environment increases heating demands.
uncertainty: MEDA temperatures are archived measurements. The controller failure and crop yields are gameplay assumptions.

title: Habitat Pressure Leak
explanation: One habitat is losing air pressure. Having oxygen in storage is different from keeping a room safely pressurized.
concept: A leak reduces cabin pressure. Isolating a section or relocating people preserves safe living volume.
uncertainty: The pressure-loss model is simplified. Its safety thresholds are game rules, not astronaut medical limits.

title: Communication Delay
explanation: The crew needs guidance on a maintenance procedure. Signals take minutes to reach Earth, and the reply takes time too.
concept: Radio waves travel at light speed, but interplanetary distances still create delays. Crews need practiced contingency procedures.
uncertainty: Signal delay stays within the documented range. An additional 60 minutes of planning is a gameplay assumption.
